reconcile.note: Clarke computes Ishmael's age at roughly seventeen when Hagar was sent away, arguing the shoulder-carrying language applies to the food and water, not to Ishmael himself.

discrepancy.note: Colenso, citing Boehmer, argues the redactor conflated E's toddler Ishmael carried by Hagar with a source making him a full-grown lad.

quotes.text: E., regards Ishmael as quite a little cliild, wlio could be carried by his mother … makes Ishmael a full-grown lad, and gives him also the blame of mocking Sarah
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), citing F. W. Boehmer, p. 208, on Genesis 21:14-20.

sides.snippet: Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
sides.verseText: Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

sides.snippet: …putting it on her shoulder, and gave her the child, and sent her away.
sides.verseText: Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and gave her the child, and sent her away. She departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
